A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpargeAttention work. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.4, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-quality, attention-speed and generation-latency experiments, plus permutation, self-similarity and sparsity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparisons in Tables 1–2 and the additional experiments and analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 15 changes the compute condition from max(m_local[I_w] - m_ij[I_w]) < λ to > λ. This locally corrects the written procedure to agree with the existing skip rule in Section 3.4 and Figure 3. The PDFs do not establish a change to the implementation used for experiments.

E1.justification: Both retain WikiText, LongBench, InfiniteBench En.MC, Needle-in-a-Haystack, Open-Sora prompts and COCO evaluations across the same language, image and video models. Appendix A.3's shorter-context evaluation is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments: full attention, MInference and FlexPrefill in Tables 1 and 11, SageAttention in Table 2, and the same kernel implementations in Figure 10. Newly cited attention methods are not added to evaluations.

E3.justification: The versions retain the same model configurations, context lengths, metrics, calibration thresholds and evaluation procedures in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, including the permutation settings and filtered-case selection rule.

E4.justification: Prediction-overhead, permutation, self-similarity, mask-contribution and sequence-length analyses are unchanged, as are the appendix case studies and diffusion sparsity analyses. The added sentence in A.4 introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Run, seed and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. Both retain the five-prompt description in A.1 and the threshold-based selection of approximately 2% of tensor cases in A.2; no statistical tests or uncertainty estimates are added.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plots and generated examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, SpargeAttn retains 708.1 TOPS and 0.909 NIAH accuracy in Table 1, and 443.6 TOPS and 0.863 NIAH accuracy in Table 11.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, Equations 1–6 and the softmax derivation in Section 3.4 are unchanged. The corrected execution guard in Algorithm 1 implements the previously stated reasoning; it introduces no revised derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of universal, training-free sparse and quantized attention, using a two-stage filter to accelerate language, image and video models without sacrificing end-to-end metrics.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly states that the existing sparsity analyses can help design diffusion algorithms. This adds a brief applicability interpretation with citations, while the existing mechanism explanations, result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed CUDA implementation, kernel fusion, calibration thresholds, GPU information and Appendix A.1's block sizes and permutation instructions are retained. The repository information and note about an updated SageAttention2 implementation are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations to sliding-tile and trainable sparse attention, and A.4 adds seven diffusion-related works. These extend existing citation coverage without substantially revising the related-work discussion or novelty positioning. Other bibliography edits update metadata or citation suffixes.

P1.justification: There are limited introductory wording edits, one added sentence in A.4 and citation/bibliographic updates. The section organization and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Captions for Tables 8 and 9 move from below to above their tables. References reflow across pages 10–12, and the added A.4 sentence slightly shifts Figures 14–16. The figure designs, table structures and displayed evidence are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1's reversed guard removes a concrete inconsistency with Section 3.4 and Figure 3, making the algorithm description more reliable to implement. Citation coverage and appendix caption consistency receive small refinements. The empirical evidence and theoretical analysis remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
